message.content: {"rules":["An Allocator implementation must handle zero-sized allocations even if its underlying allocator does not support them or returns a null pointer for them; the implementation must catch those cases.","Memory blocks currently allocated by an allocator must point to valid memory and remain valid until the block is deallocated or the allocator is dropped. A block is currently allocated when its starting address was previously returned by allocate, grow, or shrink and it has not subsequently been deallocated. Calling deallocate, or grow or shrink returning Ok, deallocates the old block; grow or shrink returning Err does not.","Copying, cloning, or moving an allocator must not invalidate memory blocks returned from it.","A copied or cloned allocator must behave like the original allocator.","A block currently allocated by an allocator may be passed to any method of that allocator that accepts such an argument. This permission applies when the block's starting address was previously returned by allocate, grow, or shrink and the block has not subsequently been deallocated by deallocate or by grow or shrink returning Ok; grow or shrink returning Err does not deallocate the block."]}
